links.note: Synonyms for परमात्मा -- ईश्वर, प्रभु. The story uses the word once, in 'सुजान सिंह बूढ़े हुए तो उन्हें परमात्मा की याद आई', the opening of 32563. 32574's MCQ lists 'परमात्मा की याद' as one option among four, but the word's home is the resignation scene.

Synonyms for प्रसिद्ध -- विख्यात, मशहूर. The word occurs in 'देश के प्रसिद्ध पत्रों में विज्ञापन निकला', which opens 32565. 32581 re-quotes that clause only to ask who would have placed the advertisement.

Synonyms for उत्साह -- जोश, जुनून. The story's only उत्साह is 'खेल बड़े उत्साह से जारी था', inside the hockey block that 32568 opens with the नए फ़ैशन वालों' proposal. 32569 picks up at संध्या with the exhaustion, पसीने से तर, not with the enthusiasm.

Synonyms for संदेह -- शक, संशय. संदेह occurs in 'युवक को संदेह हुआ कि कहीं यह सुजान सिंह तो नहीं', in 32571. 32576's खोजबीन asks students to find the sentences proving he guessed the farmer's identity; the word itself is 32571's.

Synonyms for हृदय -- मन, दिल. हृदय is the first word of 32573's own name and of Sujan Singh's specification, 'जिसके हृदय में दया हो और साथ-साथ आत्मबल'. 32570 says the young man had दया in his heart, but the word is load-bearing in the speech.

What दीवान सरदार सुजानसिंह requested of the king -- release from राज-काज. That is 32563's resignation, with the नेकनामी argument behind it. 32574's MCQ asks which of four stated reasons is the main one; this asks what he asked for.
The शर्त the king attached to accepting the resignation -- that he find the new दीवान himself, which is exactly 32564. 32563 is the request; 32564 is the condition that turns him into the examiner.

Who helps the किसान get the cart out of the नाला -- a hockey player. 32570 is that man: the one with दया and साहस who, himself limping from an injury, took off his coat and offered. 32569 ends with the players walking past with no sympathy at all.

What the युवक used to get the cart across -- हौसला. 32571 is the act: he heaved the wheel, sank knee-deep in कीचड़ and 'हिम्मत न हारी'. 32570 covers only the decision to help, before any effort was made.
What happened as the किसान's cart crossed the नाला -- it stuck in the कीचड़. 32569 is the stuck-cart scene: no bridge, mud, a steep bank, weak bullocks. 32571 is the extraction that follows.

Whom the युवक jokingly asked for an इनाम -- the किसान, from 'युवक ने हँसकर कहा, अब मुझे कुछ इनाम देते हो?' in 32571. 32573's darbar is where a reward is actually conferred, but nobody asks for one there.
What the किसान gave him -- a blessing, 'नारायण चाहेंगे तो दीवानी आपको ही मिलेगी', in 32571. 32573 is where the दीवानी is actually granted; here it is only the farmer's blessing.

With what look the युवक regarded the किसान after that grave reply -- संदेह भरी, because he wondered 'क्या यह सुजान सिंह तो नहीं'. That doubt is 32571's. 32576's खोजबीन asks for the sentences that show it, not for the look itself.

What colours crossed the उम्मीदवार faces on selection day -- आशा और निराशा, 32572's own line 'प्रत्येक के चेहरे पर आशा तथा निराशा के रंग आते-जाते थे'. 32567's candidates are performing virtue during the month, not waiting for a verdict.

Quotes the विज्ञापन and asks what it was for, what would be weighed (विद्या का कम, कर्तव्य का अधिक), what was and was not required, and what मंदाग्नि means -- 32565 is that advertisement, conditions included. 32566 is the country's reaction to it, not its text.

Quotes the तहलका paragraph -- सैकड़ों आदमी, एमामे and चोगे, and the सनद line -- and its sub-questions ask what सनद means and what the mood in the country was. 32566 is that paragraph, including the graduates' ironic reason for turning up. 32565 is the advertisement itself.

Opens on 32568's own closing lines -- the game being निराली in देवगढ़, शतरंज and ताश the serious games -- and sub-question (ग) asks exactly that. 32569 supplies the पसीने and बेदम detail but its real subject starts after the match, at the नाला.

Quotes the किसान's thanks, the joke about an इनाम, the doubt about सुजानसिंह and 'गहरे पानी में पैठने से ही मोती मिलता है' -- 32571 end to end. 32580 turns that saying into the कहावतें exercise; here it is read in place.
Quotes सुजानसिंह's speech -- दया plus आत्मबल, and the बधाई to पंडित जानकीनाथ -- and every sub-question is inside it. 32572 sets the darbar up; this passage is the speech, which is 32573.

Quotes the resignation paragraph; four of its five sub-questions are 32563's -- what he asked for, the चालीस साल of service, what he feared (नेकनामी मिट्टी में मिल जाना) and what he requested. Only the शर्त sub-question reaches into 32564.

A second copy of the तहलका paragraph, with sub-questions on what attracted people, who came from where and what kind of men appeared -- all 32566. 32582's नया फ़ैशन and पुराना चलन block borrows one clause from it for a table about the student's own home, which this item does not touch.

Quotes the stuck-cart paragraph -- no pul, कीचड़, the high bank, weak bullocks, the किसान in बड़ी आपत्ति, the players strolling up with डंडे -- and every sub-question stays inside it. 32570 begins with the one man who stops.

Quotes the extraction itself -- the wheel heaved, knees buried in mud, the cart up over the नाला, then the इनाम joke and the मोती saying -- which is 32571. 32569 is the failure before he arrives; 32570 is only the offer of help.

Begins with the दरबार being arranged, the रईस and कर्मचारी taking their seats and the candidates' कलेजे धड़कना, and sub-questions 3 and 5 ask who attended and why सुजानसिंह rose -- all of which 32572 covers, including his standing up to ask forgiveness. 32573 is the content of the speech that follows, which this item's other sub-questions borrow.

Whom the दीवान told not to apply, and why -- the मंदाग्नि patient, because हृष्ट-पुष्ट होना आवश्यक था. Both clauses are in 32565's advertisement. 32573's specification is दया and आत्मबल, not physical fitness.

What sort of उम्मीदवार मिस्टर 'अ' was -- the man who slept till nine and now strolls in the garden to watch ऊषा. He exists only in 32567's lettered roll of pretenders. 32583's 'अच्छा दिखना और अच्छा होना' generalises the behaviour; this asks about the man.

What मिस्टर 'ल' hated -- किताब, though he now sits over बड़े-बड़े ग्रंथ. Same lettered roll, 32567. 32566's graduates and their सनद are a different joke, about paper qualifications rather than pretended habits.

What the युवक saw on his way home after the game -- the helpless किसान and his cart. 32570 is that moment, 'अकस्मात उसकी निगाह गाड़ी पर पड़ी, वह ठिठक गया', with his own foot injured. 32569 describes the cart's plight before anyone notices it.

The उम्मीदवार state after the match -- पसीने से तर, खून की गरमी, हाँफते-हाँफते बेदम, which 32569 records. 32577 quotes the same sentence as its example of चित्रात्मक भाषा; this item asks for the fact, not the technique.

What the राज दरबार was like when the appointment was to be announced -- the evening court, रईस and धनाढ्य, रंग-बिरंगी सज-धज, hearts pounding. That description is 32572's. 32573 is what was then said from the floor.

The reason सुजानसिंह gave for choosing पंडित जानकीनाथ -- that a man who, himself wounded, hauled a poor किसान's loaded cart out of the दलदल has साहस, आत्मबल and उदारता. That reasoning is 32573's closing. 32570 is the deed; this is the verdict passed on it.
How many years he served the रियासत -- चालीस, from 'दास ने भी आपकी सेवा चालीस साल तक की' in 32563. 32564 holds the king's response and has no count of years.
On what शर्त the king decided to accept the त्यागपत्र -- that he find a successor himself, 32564's condition. 32563 is the request that provoked it.
Which game the उम्मीदवार proposed -- हॉकी, and 32568 is where the नए फ़ैशन वाले propose it on the reasoning 'यह भी तो आख़िर एक विद्या है'. 32569 is the match's end and the cart in the नाला.

What the उम्मीदवार were not bound by -- सनद, the word 32566 turns on, 'सनद की कैद न होने पर भी सनद से पर्दा तो ढका रहता है'. 32565's advertisement says a degree is not required; the सनद epigram itself is 32566's.

What पढ़े-लिखे लोग usually played -- शतरंज और ताश, in 32568's remark that दौड़-कूद games were thought to be children's games. 32583's वाद-विवाद asks whether hockey counts as a विद्या; this is the factual recall.

Asks which शाश्वत मूल्य the lesson defines, and the model answer runs on अच्छा आचरण and परोपकार -- that is 32583's second question, whether appearing good differs from being good, which the concept itself calls the whole story's essence. 32573 names दया and आत्मबल as the post's requirements; this asks what the story teaches the reader.
